pulls.title: Keep smart resume working when the reader opens before chapters refresh
pulls.body:
Smart resume could skip itself when you opened the reader before the details screen finished refreshing the chapter list, for example by tapping a new-chapter notification and hitting Continue straight away. You'd land on the end of the chapter you'd already finished instead of the new one.

"Wait for chapter updates" is now the default behavior and the setting is dropped. In its place is a timeout setting. This also fixes stale chapters causing a regression in where smart resume picks up.

pulls.title: Rework the history tab, updates map and navigation dock
pulls.body:
Rough first pass at a UI rework of the history tab, the Updated and Feed screens, and the navigation dock. This is not yet a proposal, it's a VERY rough draft of several designs I'm working on. I'm putting this up as a draft for both feedback and ideas, and the APK for testing. Expect a lot of changes everywhere before it's ready.

## History

The history tab can switch between views. The old list is still there as one of them.

- **Recent:** recently read manga, weighted by how much you've been reading them.
- **Calendar:** a month view; picking a day shows what you read then.
- **Shelf:** manga as spines, straight or askew, and tapping one pulls it out.

Reading statistics stay off by default, so each view has a fallback for when they're off.

## Updated and Feed

Both screens get a Map/List toggle against the existing list.

- The map is a treemap sized by new-chapter count, grouped by source or genre.
- Tiles that don't fit collapse into a "+N" tile, and tapping it drills in. Back zooms out.
- A row of small covers above the map shows recently updated manga. A new tracker setting picks whether that means the latest check or the last 24 hours.

## Dock

Continue moves from the floating button into the bottom navigation dock and follows the selected color scheme. It shows under the same conditions as the old button. `MainActionButtonBehavior` is removed because nothing needs it now.

There's also a new **Minimal theme** setting, off by default, that shrinks the dock to icons only.

pulls.title: feat(novel): implement dynamic LNReader bridge and plugin manager
pulls.body:
## Summary of Changes
This pull request integrates the **Dynamic LNReader Bridge** into Futon, adding comprehensive novel reading capabilities alongside manga:

### 1. LNReader Plugin Runtime & Manager
- **QuickJS Isolated Execution (\LnPluginRuntime\ & \LnPluginRuntimeManager\):** Directly runs official LNReader plugins (\3.0.0\ specification) inside isolated QuickJS contexts. Singletons are pooled per \pluginId\ and explicitly closed on update/uninstall to eliminate native memory leaks.
- **Remote Repository Sync (\LnPluginManager\):** Fetches and updates plugins from the official community repository (\LNReader/lnreader-plugins\).
- **Local Bundle Management (\LnPluginStorage\):** Handles local installation, version tracking, ID validation (\^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$\ rejecting \..\), and atomic disk writes (\.tmp\ file rename).

### 2. Runtime Environment Shim (\ln_env.js\)
- Pre-bundled Cheerio, htmlparser2, and dayjs for zero native overhead (documented in \ssets/lnreader/README.md\ with MIT notices).
- HTTP Fetch API bridging to OkHttp (\ etchApi\, \ etchText\) preserving request headers, cookies, redirect reflection (\esponse.url\ for Madara hostname verification), form-urlencoded \URLSearchParams\, and multipart \FormData\.
- Polyfilled globals: \console\ (bridged to Android Logcat via \__futon_native_log\), \URL\ (with \origin\ and \searchParams\), \FormData\, \NovelStatus\, and \FilterTypes\.
- Automatic default options generation (\showLatestNovels: false\, pre-populated \ ilters\), resolving parameter destructuring errors across plugins (e.g., BoxNovel, Novel Bin, Novel Fire).

### 3. Dynamic Pagination & Reader Sanitization
- **Dynamic Paging (\NovelPaginator\):** Dynamic offset-to-page tracking handles arbitrary plugin page sizes without duplication or skipped entries.
- **HTML Sanitization (\NovelChapterContent\):** Output cleaned through Jsoup \Safelist.relaxed()\ preserving furigana/ruby and image lazy-loading attributes (\srcset\, \data-src\, \data-original\) while stripping scripts and event handlers.

### 4. Mode Separation & UI Integration
- Clean separation between Manga Mode and Novel Mode in the Explore screen:
  - Manga mode displays only manga sources.
  - Novel mode displays installed LNReader novel sources and provides quick access to the Novel sources manager.
- Added \NovelPluginsManagerActivity\ with plugin search, installation, progress indicators, update badges, and uninstallation.
- Lifecycle and animation cleanups to avoid memory leaks.

## Plugin Network Trust Model
LNReader plugins execute in an isolated QuickJS JavaScript engine without filesystem or direct OS access. Network calls made by plugins bridge through Futon's shared OkHttpClient (preserving cookies, redirect URLs, and headers necessary for Cloudflare verification on novel sites). Similar to Tachiyomi / Mihon community extensions, installed LNReader plugins operate under a user-trusted external source model.

## Testing & Verification
- Unit tests executed and passing (\./gradlew testDebugUnitTest\ – 184 tests passed).
- Full debug build verification completed (\./gradlew assembleDebug\).
- Tested end-to-end popular novels, chapter parsing, and search queries.

pulls.title: Keep disabled and unused sources out of search suggestions
pulls.body:
Fixes #117

When you tap the search bar without typing, the recent sources row could show sources that were never enabled. On a fresh install every source's "last used" time is 0, so the list was just whatever the database returned first, disabled ones included.

The recent sources query now only returns sources you've actually used, and only enabled ones (unless "all sources enabled" is on). Two files, three lines: `MangaSourcesDao.findLastUsed` and `MangaSourcesRepository.getTopSources`.

Tests pass and compile, but I'm making assumptions this is what the issue is reporting got fixed, gonna stay a draft until they respond and let me know

pulls.title: fix: Keep reading statistics when migrating to another source
pulls.body:
Fixes #127

Important because this could be worse with #137

Migrating a title moved its favorites, history and tracking to the new manga id, but not its reading stats. The `stats` rows stayed on the old id, so the migrated title showed no reading time, and the rows were deleted for good once the old history was purged.

`StatsDao.move()` now reassigns them, inside the same transaction as the history move. It uses `UPDATE OR IGNORE`, so if the new title already has a session with the same start time, that row stays on the old id instead of making the migration fail.

#137 adds single and batch source replacement on top of `MigrateUseCase`, so without this a batch migration would reset stats for many titles at once.

Tests pass but I have not tested on device yet.

pulls.title: Major Kotatsu-Redo port: tracker, reader, Cloudflare, library, sources and more
pulls.body:
This PR ports over several QoL Kotatsu-Redo features and fixes that were also missing in Futon. Below is a summary of what is contained; most features and fixes can be stripped out.

## Downloads, backups and local storage

Five small, independent fixes for downloads, backups and local storage. The temp-file, decimal-settings and local-index fixes are ported from Kotatsu-Redo.

**Downloads: queued chapters were silently dropped.** Each manga's download is enqueued as unique work with `KEEP`, and the scheduler only waited while that work was RUNNING. If an earlier download of the same manga was still ENQUEUED or BLOCKED (for example, waiting for charging or an unmetered network), the next queue entry was discarded by `KEEP` and then removed from the queue, so its chapters were lost. Such entries now stay queued until the earlier download finishes, and an entry is removed only once its work is stored.

**Downloads: concurrent downloads deleted each other's temp files.** Two downloads to the same storage directory cleaned up each other's temp files. Each download now only removes its own.

**Backup: restoring sources added to the current selection instead of replacing it.** Keeps the welcome logic from interfering with restoring sources. Covered by a new case in `AppBackupAgentTest`.

**Backup: decimal settings failed to load after restoring a JSON backup.** JSON backups bring decimal values back as `Double`, which `putAll` skipped, and a value stored with the wrong type made `getFloat` throw. `putAll` now stores doubles as floats, and the decimal reader settings (double-page sensitivity, brightness/contrast, autoscroll speed and others) read through a helper that recovers a wrongly-typed value.

**Local storage: the index rebuild blocked the database on cold start.** The storage scan ran inside the index rebuild transaction and held Room's write connection the whole time. The scan now runs first, and the transaction only writes the results.

## Suggestions and related manga

Ported from Kotatsu-Redo, local parts only, with a few changes noted below.

**Fixes**
- **The suggestions worker kept the least relevant suggestions.** It sorted ascending by relevance, so it kept the wrong end. The notification picker also crashed with fewer than 3 suggestions (`Random.nextInt(0, 0)`).
- **Related manga ignored "disable NSFW".** NSFW titles now stay hidden when NSFW content is disabled.

**Smarter suggestions**
- Seed tags are now the reader's most telling tags, weighted by how rare each tag is across the local library (TF-IDF), rather than simply the most frequent ones. Blacklisted tags are never used as seeds.
- Dropped manga (barely read, untouched for 3 weeks, not a favourite) no longer feed suggestions.
- A source is never searched without a tag (that would return its whole catalogue). Two matched tags are searched together where the source supports it, falling back to one.
- Rating sort is preferred over popularity.
- Unlike Redo, suggestions stay **off by default**, so existing users who never opted in don't get a new background worker hitting every enabled source.

**Related manga fallback**
When a source links fewer than four related titles, the row is filled from the reader's stored suggestions that share this manga's tags, weighted by rarity. If that's still short, it's filled from one search of the manga's own source for its rarest tags. NSFW and the tag blacklist are respected. Extension sources skip the source search, because their shared repository has stateful paging. The related-list screen uses the same logic. Redo's community-server part is left out.

Covered by the new `SuggestionRankingTest`.

## Webtoon reader

Three webtoon reader fixes, ported from Kotatsu-Redo.

**Broken page sizing.** Pages could collapse to zero height, render hugely zoomed in (infinite scale), or get cut off.

**Pages cut off at page joins.** A scroll now walks every page it reaches instead of only the first two, so a fast fling over short pages can no longer carry a tall page past the edge of the screen with its image unscrolled. Each page's inner scroll is re-pinned after every layout (decode, zoom, rotation). A page that finishes decoding after it has already scrolled partly off screen is placed without jumping to its end or moving what's on screen.

**Pull-to-switch-chapter gesture rewritten.** The EdgeEffect-based pull is replaced by a touch tracker that only starts a pull when both the list and the edge page's image are really at their first or last edge. The edge glow is turned off while the gesture is enabled. The feedback chip fades in from 0.15 to full opacity, switches to an outlined background once the threshold is reached, and hides as soon as you let go.

## Tracker

Several fixes to how chapter progress is saved, to protect progress from being lost, and to how new chapters are fetched.

**Counting fixes**
- **Tracks reset or stuck.** Tracks shared by history and favourites no longer have their baseline reset on every run, and sources with update checks disabled no longer hold batch slots forever.
- **New chapters not credited.** Opening the reader on an older chapter moved the tracked chapter to the newest one without counting what had been released since. Those chapters now show up in Updates.
- **Sources that change chapter URLs.** When the tracked chapter is gone from the fresh list, the comparison falls back to its upload date, then to the history chapter, before re-baselining. A track's first check anchors on the history chapter.
- **Read and old chapters reported as new.** Chapters at or before the reading position (including the same title read on another source), or uploaded more than 90 days ago, are no longer reported.
- **Long-inactive tracks.** Tracks with no new chapter, read or favourite in 90 days drop out of regular checks but are still checked weekly. Stale unread counters are cleared.
- **Clearing updates** now resets each track to the history chapter, so unread chapters are recomputed from the reading position.
- **Manual checks** check every track even when the system refuses a foreground service.
- **One-time recovery** for tracks that were already advanced past unread chapters. It runs on first launch with network, needs no schema change, and is gated by two preference flags.

**Throughput and save fixes** (Not a port: New feat/fix)
- **Per-source limit.** At most 2 checks run per source, within the existing 6. The source slot is taken before the global one, so a busy source can't hold global slots while it waits.
- **Blocked sources.** After a source's first Cloudflare or rate-limit (429) failure, its remaining manga in the run aren't requested. They're stamped as checked in one update, so a blocked source can't fill the next batches either.
- **No network inside the save transaction.** Progress refresh could fetch pages while holding the save transaction open. It now runs after the save, and a failed refresh no longer fails a check that was already saved.
- The last-chapter date now comes from the tracked branch rather than from all branches.

**Re-check after a captcha solve** (Not a port: New feat/fix)
- Captcha failures are stored as a new result, `RESULT_CAPTCHA` (5). `last_result` is a plain int, so no migration is needed.
- Each successful solve queues one re-check of that source's captcha-blocked tracks. Solves come from the captcha notification, or from the automatic solver if that lands. It uses the existing `CaptchaHandler.discard()`, so it doesn't depend on any other PR.
- It can't loop: a re-check that hits the captcha again only shows the notification.
- New setting: "Re-check after solving a CAPTCHA", on by default.

**New Features Ported**
- Swipe to remove a feed item, with undo.
- New "Recently read manga" download strategy: new chapters of manga read in the last 30 days are downloaded, up to 5 per manga per run. Nothing is queued with less than 2 GB free or when the download quota is reached. Tracker downloads now go through the download queue, so the Wi-Fi, charging and off-peak settings apply to them. (Modified: in Redo the 5-chapter cap also hit the existing "Downloaded manga" strategy, so chapters over the cap were never downloaded; here only the new strategy is capped.)

## Cloudflare

Fixes to how the app gets through Cloudflare, plus an experimental opt-in automatic captcha solver. Most of this is ported from Kotatsu-Redo.

**Fixes**
- **Request interception broke after a Cloudflare interstitial.** The page script was injected only once, so captures timed out when a challenge page came before the real one. It's now re-injected on every navigation and polled while capturing. Captures are serialised and reuse a single WebView, and evaluation WebViews are now destroyed after use, so they no longer leak.
- **The clearance cookie didn't match the User-Agent.** If the solver WebView had a non-Android User-Agent, Turnstile could fail. The UA is now realigned with the engine's default, and the one that earned clearance is stored per source, so OkHttp sends the agent the `cf_clearance` cookie is bound to.
- **The user's own User-Agent setting wins** (Modified). If the user changes the source's User-Agent setting, the stored clearance agent is ignored. In Redo the stored agent was never cleared and silently overrode the user's setting.

**Automatic captcha solving (experimental, off by default)**
- New global switch under Storage and network: "Solve CAPTCHAs automatically (experimental)". It's **off by default**, and there's also a per-source opt-out.
- When it's on, opening a catalog, a manga or a chapter first tries to pass the challenge silently, in a translucent WebView activity. A read-only page-state probe decides when the real page has loaded.
- Only one session runs at a time. Cooldowns are 30 s after a success and 3 min after a failure. It only starts while the app is in the foreground and is cancelled when it goes to the background. Background workers, prefetch and image loading never start a solve.
- The headless `WebViewExecutor.tryResolveCaptcha` path and its two WebView clients are removed, because `CaptchaHandler` was their only user. AdBlock is kept.
- It's marked experimental because it can't solve interactive challenges, and every challenge I got while testing was interactive. It should pass non-interactive ones, but I haven't been able to confirm that.

## Library

- **Progress badges** no longer show a leading "-" on "percent left" and "chapters left".
- **Hide NSFW from launcher shortcuts:** a new setting, on by default. NSFW titles are also left out of shortcuts whenever NSFW content is disabled.
- **Pin favourites.** Pin or unpin from the favourites selection mode. Pinned entries sort first under every sort order and show a pin badge in grid and detailed list modes. A manga pinned in any list counts as pinned in the all-favourites view, and pinning from that view pins it in every list it's in. It uses the existing `favourites.pinned` column, so no migration is needed.
- **Quick filters for favourites:** Manga / Manhwa / Manhua chips, plus the three most common tags of the current list. Tags are matched by title, so the same genre from different sources is one chip, and blacklisted tags aren't offered. Mihon sources report everything as plain manga, so their content type comes from a manga/manhwa/manhua genre tag. A Mihon title without one is only listed when no content-type chip is selected, instead of being misfiled under "Manga".
- **Search within History and Favourites.** On the History and Favourites screens, the search bar can now search just that screen. An option in the search bar switches between normal search and "History" or "Favourites". In screen mode, typing filters the list you're looking at instead of opening a new search. It matches the manga's title (including alternative titles), its source, and for favourites, the list it's in. While the filter is active it stays visible in the search bar with a button to clear it, and it's cleared automatically when you leave the screen.
  - Changes from Redo: it also works with Mihon sources, the search text is passed to the database safely rather than pasted into the query, and the Downloaded view is filtered the same way.

Covered by the new `ContentTypeConditionTest` and `LibrarySearchTest`.

## Sources and alternatives

- **"Content unavailable" dialog.** When a manga's source says it's gone (404 or removed), the app now says so and offers a shortcut to search for it on other sources. This also works with Mihon extension sources.
- **Source presets.** Save named sets of languages and sources, and switch between them from Explore. While a preset is active, Explore and global search use only its sources, and adding or removing sources in the catalog edits the preset rather than your enabled sources. Uninstalled sources and deleted presets are handled cleanly. The active preset survives a settings backup and restore.
  - This adds a new database table, `source_presets` (migration 30 → 31). Note for sync: requests will now send `X-Db-Version: 31`.
- **Replace source** (Modified). "Fix" in the favourites and history selection menus becomes "Replace source", and it's also in the manga details menu. It checks every candidate source against your library titles from the old source, lets you pick the best one, and moves the matches over automatically. Unlike Redo, it asks before replacing every matched title. Anything it can't match, you choose by hand. Each title is migrated on its own, so one failure doesn't stop the rest.
- **Search options for alternatives.** The alternatives screen gets options for:
  - which sources to search (enabled, disabled, or a preset)
  - same language only
  - same content type only
  - hiding results without chapters
  - four sort orders
  - an editable search query
  - a progress counter
- **Covers from other sources.** The manga edit screen can pick a cover from other sources. Duplicate covers are filtered out, and the chosen cover is saved locally.

I did not port Redo's community ranking system.

## JPEG XL

Ported from Kotatsu-Redo.
- JPEG XL images now display everywhere: covers, thumbnails, previews and reader pages. They're detected by their content as well as by the `.jxl` extension.
- If the JPEG XL library fails to load on a device, only JPEG XL images fail; nothing else is affected.
- **New dependency:** `io.github.awxkee:jxl-coder` 2.6.1. It bundles native libraries for each CPU type and adds about 11 MB to the debug APK (48.7 → 59.8 MB). It's a large dependency for a niche feature, so it's up to you whether it's worth adding.

## Reader and history

- **Reading position kept when a source changes chapter IDs.** Some sources give chapters new IDs between loads, which used to lose your place. The history now follows the same chapter in the new list (matched by URL, then volume and number). If it can't be matched, the position is estimated within the branch you were reading, not across all branches. If your history chapter is gone entirely, progress is rescaled to the new chapter count instead of being dropped; that estimate only ever lowers progress, and never marks a manga as completed.
- **Default branch re-picked** once the fresh chapter list loads, not only from the cached one, so a recovered position opens in the right branch.
- **Smart resume fix** (Not a port: New feat/fix). Continue reopened the finished chapter after a new release instead of moving on, because the progress recalculation overwrote the chapter count that smart resume relies on. The count is left to the reader again.
- **Double-page rework.**
  - Two chapters never share a spread.
  - New option "First page as cover (solo)" shows each chapter's first page on its own.
  - Pinch-zoom and pan now work on the whole spread instead of one page at a time.
  - Pages are centred against each other instead of the screen edges.
  - Wide images span the full spread.
  - Right-to-left mode gets identical spreads.
- **E-Ink flash on page change.** An optional full-screen white or black flash on page change clears ghosting on E-Ink screens. Duration and frequency are configurable. It doesn't flash when opening a manga, switching reader mode, or during webtoon autoscroll.

Overlaps with #118 in `DoubleReaderFragment` and `ReversedDoubleReaderFragment`; I'll rebase whichever lands second.

## Testing

Unit tests pass (157, 0 failures) and the debug build succeeds. `AppBackupAgentTest` and `ProgressUpdateRaceTest` are instrumented tests and weren't run.

I tested all of these together and confirmed they work on my device (S26). Automatic captcha solving is the exception: it couldn't be verified, since every challenge I got was interactive.

pulls.title: ci: fix broken CI builds on forked PRs
pulls.body:
This fixes successful builds that report "failed" because they couldn't create a comment, and therefore report a total failure.

GitHub gives pull_request runs from a fork a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN,
whatever the workflow asks for, so issues.createComment is refused and
the job is marked failed although the APK built and was uploaded.

The comment step now only runs for pull requests from branches in this repository, so fork PRs still build and upload the APK but skip the comment.

pulls.title: feat(settings): add custom theme import and dynamic theming support
pulls.body:
## Summary
Adds support for creating, importing, managing, and applying custom user themes via JSON files (Idle Fantasy Material 3 compatible format). 

Users can now import custom palette files, select their imported themes from a dedicated dialog or the existing color scheme carousel, and have their chosen seed colors dynamically applied throughout the application on Android 6.0+ (API 23+).

---

## Why this is needed
- **Personalization**: Users were previously restricted to built-in presets (Miku, Asuka, Totoro, etc.) or system Monet (Android 12+ only).
- **Universal Dynamic Theming**: Allows users on older Android versions (API 23–31) to enjoy content-based Material dynamic theming derived from their custom theme seed colors using Material Color Utilities without requiring OS Monet engine support.
- **Interoperability**: Supports importing JSON palette definitions from community tools.

---

## What was done
1. **JSON Parsing & Validation (`ImportedTheme.kt`)**:
   - Implemented a parser validating schema, size limits (≤ 256 KB), color format (hex/argb), base mode (`light` / `dark`), and extraction of primary seed and contrast colors.
2. **Settings & In-Memory Caching (`AppSettings.kt`)**:
   - Added `importedThemes`, `selectedCustomThemeId`, `importCustomThemes()`, and `deleteCustomTheme()`.
   - Built with an in-memory `@Volatile` cache to avoid re-parsing JSON on every property access, preserving strict performance requirements (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
3. **Application Theming (`BaseActivity.kt`)**:
   - Applied custom seed color dynamic theming using `DynamicColors.applyToActivityIfAvailable` with `DynamicColorsOptions.Builder().setContentBasedSource(...)`.
   - Operates universally on Android 6.0–14+ without gating behind `isDynamicColorAvailable()`.
4. **Theme Preference & Management UI (`ThemeChooserPreference.kt`, `AppearanceSettingsFragment.kt`)**:
   - Added preferences to import theme files, switch between custom themes, and delete themes.
   - Handled file reading asynchronously on `Dispatchers.IO` using `runCatchingCancellable` to prevent UI thread blockage/ANRs during cloud storage imports.
   - Handled proper activity recreation (`postRestart()`) when switching between custom themes.
   - Preserved card preview shapes in `ThemeChooserPreference` by tinting shapes directly with the seed color rather than flattening the card background.

---

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
| :--- | :--- |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../core/prefs/ImportedTheme.kt` | **[New]** Theme model and JSON parser for custom palette files. |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../core/prefs/AppSettings.kt` | Persistent storage, in-memory cache, and management methods for imported custom themes. |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../core/prefs/ColorScheme.kt` | Added `CUSTOM` entry to the available color schemes list when custom themes exist. |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../core/ui/BaseActivity.kt` | Universal content-based theming via `DynamicColorsOptions.setContentBasedSource(...)`. |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../settings/AppearanceSettingsFragment.kt` | UI for file picker import, selection dialog, deletion, and coroutine-based async reading. |
| `app/src/main/kotlin/.../settings/utils/ThemeChooserPreference.kt` | Preview rendering with shape tinting and `refresh()` method. |
| `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` | String resources for custom theme management dialogs and actions. |
| `app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml` | Added `ThemeOverlay.Futon.Custom.Light` and `ThemeOverlay.Futon.Custom.Dark`. |
| `app/src/main/res/xml/pref_appearance.xml` | Added preference entries for managing, importing, and deleting custom themes. |

---

## Verification
- [x] Tested compilation via `./gradlew compileDebugKotlin` (Build succeeded).
- [x] Zero new external dependencies added (complies with `CONTRIBUTING.md` APK size rule).
- [x] File I/O executed on `Dispatchers.IO` (complies with performance rule).
- [x] Preserved docstrings and existing coding standards.

pulls.title: Keep reader history saves from landing out of order
pulls.body:
I’m currently testing this on my own device, and it’s opened as a draft so others can test it too before it’s marked ready. This goes together with #118, which fixes one source of bad saves; this one stops a bad save from sticking.

Each reader progress save (crossing into a new chapter, leaving the reader, going idle) runs as its own background task. Its database transaction also rewrites the chapter list and updates tracking. So two saves made a few milliseconds apart can reach the database in either order, and an out-of-date position can overwrite the newer one that came right after it. It’s the same kind of problem as the progress recalculation fix in #111, but for the reader’s own saves.

This adds a small HistorySaveOrder that numbers each save at the moment it’s requested. Saves are then written one at a time, and any save older than one already written for that manga is skipped, so the newest position always wins. A save that fails doesn’t count, so an older one can still go through. A skipped stale save also no longer triggers smart download for an out-of-date chapter. History changes you make yourself, like mark as read, mark as current and progress recalculation, aren’t affected.

HistorySaveOrderTest covers out-of-order saves, normal ordering, separate manga, a failed save, and two saves running at once. The full unit test suite passes.

The PR compiles and runs, but the bug is so transient and hard to reproduce on demand I’m still testing it on my end to see if this finally fixes it.

pulls.title: Fix: reader saving the previous chapter’s first page as reading progress
pulls.body:
I’m currently testing this on my own device, and it’s opened as a draft so others can test it too before it’s marked ready. This is one of two related fixes; the other is #119.

Every now and then, reopening a manga would land on the first page of the previous chapter instead of where I left off. For example, I’d be reading chapter 39 and come back to page 1 of chapter 38. It was hard to reproduce on purpose, and it seemed to happen more with smart resume on.

The cause is a short window where the reader’s saved position and what’s actually on screen disagree. When you’re on one of the first few pages of a chapter, the reader loads the previous chapter in the background and adds its pages to the front of the list. The view model starts using the new list right away, but the reader view only catches up a moment later. Page changes were reported as list positions, so if one came in during that gap, the view model looked the position up in the newer list. “Page 1 of chapter 39” became “page 1 of chapter 38”. That looked like a chapter change, so it was saved to history straight away. Smart resume makes this more likely because it opens new chapters on page 1, which is exactly when the previous chapter gets loaded in.

The fix is to report pages instead of positions. Each reader view now looks the visible pages up in its own list and passes those, and the view model finds them in its list by chapter and page number. If a page isn’t loaded any more, it does nothing instead of guessing. The reversed and double-reversed modes no longer need their own position flipping. This also covers the reverse case, where dropping a chapter from the front of a long list could shift positions the other way and save a later chapter.

The PR compiles and runs, but the bug is so transient and hard to reproduce on demand I’m still testing it on my end to see if this finally fixes it.

pulls.title: Add opt-in smart resume for newly available chapters
pulls.body:
Currently, when you're finished with a chapter and a new update is posted, you click on it and end up loading both the end of the old chapter and, inevitably, the next chapter. This PR adds an opt-in feature called smart resume that, depending on the configurable settings, will automatically skip to the new chapter's first page, making it both smoother and requiring less to load and process overall.

I feel like it could use some more feedback on the behavior, as I just designed it to fix an annoyance that goes hand in hand with the problem the [prefetch PR](https://github.com/AppFuton/Futon/pull/110) fixes.

Settings appear inline after the reader-mode controls:

- Smart resume defaults to off.
- Completion uses either percentage of pages reached (default 90%) or pages remaining (default one).
- Both thresholds accept exact whole-number entry and retain independent values.
- An optional, default-off update wait has a separate help button explaining latency and cached chapter data.

With waiting off, the first usable chapter list determines the position; later updates cannot trigger a jump.
With waiting on, potentially eligible starts wait for the normal details update without forcing a refresh.
Original history is captured before recovery or startup writes. Recovered history is ineligible. Failed updates
or empty/failed successor loads preserve the saved position; cancellation propagates.

Completion counts the current source page as reached, rather than scroll distance within a long image.
Previous-latest detection uses the saved chapter count and assumes chapters are appended in reading order.
The implementation uses existing preferences, with no database migration or new dependency.

I compiled the APK and tested it on my phone and an emulator; both are working as expected.
pulls.author: PoonHarpoon

pulls.title: Fix saved reading progress reverting to an earlier page
pulls.body:
Your saved position can move backwards after you finish reading: a chapter you reached the end of can
reopen on an earlier page and show 99% progress again, or progress can be lost or messed up entirely. This can happen when a slow progress calculation
finishes after the reader has already saved your newer position, replacing that save with older information.

Before writing a recalculated percentage, check that the saved history has not changed since the calculation
started. Keep the check and write together in a short database transaction so a newer save cannot slip
between them. The fix changes one production file, with six net added lines; existing reader save callbacks
and percentage calculations stay as they are.

I compiled the APK and tested it on my phone and an emulator; both are working as expected.

Tests added.
pulls.author: PoonHarpoon

pulls.title: Fix loading pauses between chapters when preloading is enabled
pulls.body:
With **Preload pages** enabled, pages ahead of your current position are loaded in advance. Previously,
that preload request could run before the next chapter's page list was available. When the list arrived,
the reader added it without requesting another preload. You could read smoothly through the current chapter,
then reach the next one and have to wait for its first images to load.

This change requests preloading as soon as the next chapter's page list has been added, giving its first
images time to load while you finish the current chapter. Moving into the next chapter therefore feels much
smoother: its images can already be ready instead of starting to load as you reach them. The benefit depends
on how quickly you read and how quickly the source delivers the images.

It uses the existing **Preload pages** setting and its network, battery, memory, cache, and queue limits.
Only pages from the immediately following chapter are selected, and chapters already loaded are skipped.

I compiled the APK and tested it on my phone and an emulator; both are working as expected.

Tests added to check behavior is consistent.

pulls.title: Fix app crashes on android 6
pulls.body:
We had two problems on issue #63.

## Issue 2: Android 6 "Bad position" (ICU Decoder) Bug

Android 6.0 (API 23) contains a system-level bug in the `java.nio` charset decoder (ICU). When decoding certain byte sequences from a network response into a `String`, the decoder can incorrectly flush its buffer, leading to an `IllegalArgumentException: Bad position`. This prevents the app from correctly detecting and handling Cloudflare protection on older devices.

**Current Workaround**: 
I implemented a manual byte-peeking and decoding strategy in `CloudFlareInterceptor.kt` specifically for API 23 to bypass the buggy system decoder for basic protection detection.

While our interceptor now has a safety check, the core `CloudFlareHelper` within the [kotatsu-parsers-redo](https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo/kotatsu-parsers-redo) library still relies on standard decoding methods that trigger this crash. To fully resolve this problem, [Kotatsu-Redo](https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo) team needs to update `CloudFlareHelper` to avoid triggering the ICU bug on Android 6 (e.g., by using a safer decoding approach or peeking the source).

## Issue 2: Focus Search Crash 

When hitting enter on the search bar the app would throw the following exception: `java.lang.IllegalStateException: focus search returned a view that wasn't able to take focus!`

**Solution:**
I've updated the `item_extension.xml` layout to make the root container explicitly focusable and clickable. This ensures that the list item itself serves as a stable focus target, preventing the focus-finder from failing when internal buttons disappear.

---
Fixes #63

pulls.title: Add support for mihon extensions
pulls.body:
## Overview
This change introduces support for downloading, installing, and managing Mihon-compatible extensions within Futon. It adds a dedicated Extension Manager screen under Settings, allowing users to browse, update, and remove external sources.

## Key Changes

- **Extensions Manager UI**: Created a new activity and adapter to list extensions with real-time state tracking (Installed, Update Available, Not Installed).
- **Download & Install Flow**: Implemented `ExtensionInstallService` to handle the background downloading of APKs and trigger the system installation flow.
- **In-place Actions**: Added support for:
  - **Installation/Updates**: One-tap installation of new or updated extensions.
  - **Uninstallation**: A dedicated "Uninstall" button and long-press shortcut for quick removal.
  - **Download Progress**: Integrated a `LinearProgressIndicator` within list items to show active download status.
- **Permissions**: Added `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` and `REQUEST_DELETE_PACKAGES` to the manifest to support package management on modern Android versions.

## Technical Improvements

- **StrictMode Compliance**: Fixed a `DiskWriteViolation` by moving APK file operations to Dispatchers.IO.
- **Architecture**: Followed the project's Hilt-based MVVM pattern and used `AdapterDelegates` for a modular list implementation.
- **Settings Integration**: Exposed the feature via the `"Extension Manager"` preference in the Remote Sources settings.

## Known issues

- The extensions favicon appear blank in `Manga sources` view.
- Extension name says `"Unknown"` in its catalog view
- Extension name says `"Unknown"` and its favicon appear blank in manga description.

issues.title: Storage bloat while reading (in-place PNG conversion bypasses DiskLruCache limit & v9.9 reader storage)
issues.body: ### Brief summary App storage (and HyperOS `System files -> Other`) bloats rapidly while reading and is only reclaimed when clearing all app data: 1. **In-place PNG overwrite bypasses `DiskLruCache` size limit (`PageLoader.convertBimap`)**: When `SubsamplingScaleImageView` fails with `IOException` (`PageViewModel.onImageLoadError`), `PageLoader.convertBimap(uri)` decodes the cached file and calls `image.compressToPNG(file)` directly on the file inside `DiskLruCache` (`pages/`). Re-encoding compressed images (e.g., AVIF/WebP) to lossless PNG inflates each page to several MB, while `DiskLruCache` still tracks the original `put()` byte size and never evicts past the 200 MB limit. 2. **Cache clear leaves stale `DiskLruCache` state & orphaned temp files**: - `DataCleanupSettingsViewModel.clearCache` calls `LocalStorageManager.clearCache` (`deleteRecursively()`) without calling `LocalStorageCache.clear()`, leaving the singleton `DiskLruCache` journal stale in memory. - `LocalStorageCache.createBufferFile` writes `.` into `cacheDir.parentFile` (outside `pages/`), so process death mid-download leaves orphaned temp files outside `CacheDir.PAGES`. 3. **v9.9 Novel Reader storage/DB churn**: - `NovelReaderActivity.setupWebView` enables `domStorageEnabled = true` with default `cacheMode` and loads chapters with `baseUrl = chapterUrl`, accumulating Chromium data under `app_webview/` (app data, only cleared by "Clear Data"). - `NovelReaderViewModel.updateScrollProgress` calls `historyRepository.addOrUpdate` (`ChaptersDao.replaceAll`) on every unthrottled JS scroll event. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Read chapters in Futon v9.9. 2. Observe filesystem / `System files -> Other` storage growing continuously across reading sessions (reaching ~106 GB). 3. Clear all app data for Futon in Android Settings -> bloated storage immediately disappears. ### Evidence https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28e1258d-77b0-4074-8f79-e8e2a1aa3869 ### Futon version 9.9 ### Android version Android 16 (HyperOS 3.0.307.0.WNCCNXM.C11 | Android security update: 2026-08-01) ### Device Xiaomi 14 ### Acknowledgements - [x] This is not a duplicate of an existing issue. Please look through the list of [open issues](https://github.com/AppFuton/Futon/issues) before creating a new one. - [x] This is not an issue with a specific manga source. issues.title: Sync fails with databaseError whenever the server returns library contents (HTTP 200)
issues.body:
### Brief summary

Sync with a self-hosted sync server never completes. Every sync that receives a non-empty response
fails with `SyncResult: databaseError: true`. Android treats this as a hard error and does not
retry, and nothing is written to the device — the library stays empty.

Uploads work: data added on the device reaches the server and is stored correctly. Downloads never
apply.

Observed pattern across both of my devices:

- Server responds **204 No Content** (nothing changed) → sync succeeds
- Server responds **200** with library contents → sync fails with `databaseError: true`

The server returns HTTP 200 and a well-formed body; the failure occurs on the device after the
response is received. Response times of 3.8s and 24.2s both failed identically, so it is not a
timeout.

Server: `KotatsuApp/kotatsu-syncserver` @ master, MariaDB 11.8, HTTPS via a reverse proxy.

Account data held server-side:

| | |
|---|---|
| favourites | 54 (52 not soft-deleted) |
| manga | 97 |
| tags | 190 |
| favourite categories | 4 |
| history entries | 82 |

`GET /resource/favourites` for this account returns **58,011 bytes** of JSON.

**logcat**

```
W SyncManager: failed sync operation JobId=100000 .../io.github.landwarderer.futon.sync u0
  [io.github.landwarderer.futon.favourites] OTHER ExpectedIn=-27s STANDBY-EXEMPTED(TOP)
  Reason=AutoSync, SyncResult: databaseError: true stats []
E SyncManager: not retrying sync operation because the error is a hard error:
  JobId=100000 .../io.github.landwarderer.futon.sync u0
  [io.github.landwarderer.futon.favourites] OTHER Reason=AutoSync Retries=1
```

Identical output for `io.github.landwarderer.futon.history`.

No stack trace is available: on a release build the exception is not written to logcat, so logcat
contains no entry from the app itself. There is nothing in the `crash` buffer and nothing in
`dumpsys dropbox`.

**`adb shell dumpsys content`** — after enabling both authorities:

```
Authority                                Syncable  Enabled  Tot  Fail  Time  Last Sync
io.github.landwarderer.futon.favourites  1         true     2    2     31s   USER FAILURE
io.github.landwarderer.futon.history     1         true     2    2     30s   USER FAILURE

Sync Statistics
  Today:   Success (0) Failure (4 for 61.9s avg=15.4s)
  Day-1:   Success (0) Failure (58 for 169.8s avg=2.9s)
  Week-3:  Success (0) Failure (35 for 246.4s avg=7.0s)
  Week-11: Success (0) Failure (15 for 33.1s avg=2.2s)
  Week-29: Success (0) Failure (4 for 7.0s avg=1.7s)
```

Zero successful syncs on this account, going back 29 weeks.

**Server access log for the same two attempts**

```
POST /resource/favourites 200 in 24241ms
POST /resource/history    200 in 20946ms
POST /resource/favourites 200 in  3835ms
POST /resource/history    200 in  3005ms
```

I captured the 58 KB response body and can attach it if useful.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Host `KotatsuApp/kotatsu-syncserver` and point Futon at it (Settings → Services →
   Synchronization settings → Server address)
2. Sign in, and upload a library of this size from one device — uploads succeed, and the data is
   verifiably stored server-side
3. On a second device with an empty library, sign in to the same account and sync
4. The server responds 200 with the full library; the sync fails and nothing is written locally

Reproducible on demand: two consecutive manual syncs produced the same result.

12

Looking at the "Check for new chapters log" under the settings, I see several sources that report a number of issues/exceptions. Migrating the faulty ones seems to make the worker go further when checking for new chapters.

I did a debug session and it seems like one or more tracked items ends up cancelled (**not** via a user UI action), so the whole worker batch aborts and `WorkManager` reports a `CancellationException` before the other tracked items are processed.

issues.title: MangasOrigines broken (empty chapter list) — parsers pin predates upstream fix, please bump kotatsu-parsers-redo
issues.body:
### Brief summary

Since the redesign of mangas-origines.fr (custom `ori-*` theme on top of Madara, around mid-August 2026), the **MangasOrigines** source no longer works in Futon: the manga details open but the chapter list is empty, so nothing can be read.

The fix already exists upstream in the parsers library Futon depends on:

- Kotatsu-Redo/kotatsu-parsers-redo#184 — "Fix MangasOrigines and HentaiOrigines chapter parsing after site redesign" (merged 2026-08-24, commit `6e94eaa30c`, follow-up `434030d481`)
- Shipped to Kotatsu-Redo users in [9.8.2](https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo/Kotatsu-Redo/releases/tag/9.8.2) (2026-08-25, "Fix MangasOrigines", parsers pin `434030d481`) and [9.8.3](https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo/Kotatsu-Redo/releases/tag/9.8.3) (2026-09-05, parsers pin `38cfb00b0a`)

Futon `devel` is still pinned to `parsers = "204c9ee032"` in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` (commit from 2026-08-03), which predates the fix. Futon 9.8.1 (2026-08-16) therefore ships the broken parser, and so does the current nightly.

Bumping the pin also picks up the other source fixes from the same range (Comix, RavenScans, Com-X, InkStory, Voratoon, LunarAnime, MgKomik, SoulScan, GeassComic, Desu, MangaDotNet) and the new OniSaga / Ryukomik / Chikari sources.

I checked the non-source API diff between `204c9ee032` and `38cfb00b0a`: the only change outside `site/` is an additive `MangaLoaderContext.requestCloudflareVerification()` with a default implementation, so no app-side change should be needed. Both commits are already built on JitPack.

PR with the one-line bump: #115

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Futon 9.8.1 (or a current nightly)
2. Enable the **MangasOrigines** (FR) source
3. Open any manga from that source
4. Chapter list is empty / "no chapters" — reading is impossible

### Futon version

9.8.1 (also reproduced on `devel` / nightly, parsers pin `204c9ee032`)

### Android version

Any — the issue is in the pinned parsers library, not device-specific

### Device

Any

### Acknowledgements

- [x] This is not a duplicate of an existing issue.
- [x] This is not an issue with a specific manga source in the parsers repository — the parser is already fixed upstream; this issue is about Futon's dependency pin being outdated.

issues.title: Download Scheduler - Schedule manga downloads for optimal times
issues.body:
### Describe your suggested feature

Add a download scheduler feature that allows users to automatically download chapters at specified times and under specific conditions, addressing battery drain, data plan concerns, and network congestion. Users should be able to set download schedules with trigger conditions (WiFi-only, charging-only, off-peak hours, or combinations thereof), create and prioritize download queues (drag-to-reorder), implement smart batch operations (e.g., "download all unread from favorites," "auto-download next chapter after reading"), and configure auto-cleanup rules (auto-delete oldest chapters after reading while preserving favorites, with configurable storage quotas). The feature should provide real-time queue monitoring with progress indicators, ETAs, and bandwidth throttling options, support pause/resume on individual and bulk downloads, include retry logic with exponential backoff for failed downloads, and integrate with the existing notification system. Implementation should leverage Android WorkManager for reliable background scheduling that survives reboots and respects device doze mode, store queue metadata in the local Room database, and integrate seamlessly with the existing download infrastructure. This enables users to maintain offline manga libraries passively without manual intervention or resource constraints.

issues.title: Revert Kotatsu's homophobic inclusion of queer categories in it's "highlight dangerous categories" functionality
issues.body:
### Describe your suggested feature

Created this issue which has been dealt with on Kotatsu-Redo: https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo/Kotatsu-Redo/issues/18, just spotted this fork Futon from F-droid so want to also point out to yourself.

The "Highlight dangerous categories": "Highlight genres that may be inappropriate for most users", is a function that's on by default in the "Manga sources" settings page.

The feature is homophobia guised as a "safety" feature which as can be seen from this revert commit of the feature from Kotatsu-Redo: https://github.com/Kotatsu-Redo/Kotatsu-Redo/commit/40620480df1ba36034f463e9ed8d592e1a9cfc30, it DOES contain a heck tonne of dangerous stuff (though be it even that not nearly anywhere near enough to be actually about safety what is there beyond queer tags in that long list of categories.. but you'll also find endless queer and related tags such as "Yaoi" (Boy Love) for instance as such shown in the linked issue on Kotatsu-Redo.

It's simply blatant homophobia. It's definitely not a safety feature, bundling in all the actual bad stuff was clearly an afterthought to downplay queer content being the target. If you look at the actual functionality.. all it is doing is adding a highlight on the "dangerous" tags on the associated manga's description page. It doesn't hide such "dangerous" manga from searches, from appearing when you scroll through, so hey a manga with actual gore in the cover image comes into the results, what good does this tag highlight achieve in that situation where you've already been subjected to the content.

Sure it may stop someone from clicking to read the manga if the dangerous content isn't front stage like that but in the manga.. but then the massive majority of these mangas are pretty lacking with their tags anyway. Like how many mangas have triggering aspects like regarding suicide and things amongst the story and there's nothing to suggest you're walking into that.

It's more harmful than any tiny bit of good this "highlight dangerous categories" feature. It serves only the original maintainer's homophobia because they just didn't want to accidently be stumbling upon and reading queer manga, and they just couldn't keep that to themselves.

So I would like to request to yourself as well with your fork, please revert this homophobic feature like Kotatsu-Redo maintainer had done so. Queerphobia has no place.

Better functionality for "safety" is categorising sources by safe to nsfw to dangerous etc, with dangerous sources disabled by default.. aka the obscure sources you probably are going to go out your way anyway to stumble on the vast majority of those actual morbid tags in that dangerous categories list since the more reputable sources just doesn't have those kinds of tags. Other functionality would be keyword filtering functionality you can put whatever you want to filter what you don't want.. but then as like mentioned on the linked issue, that's going to not really be viable due to you'd immediately run into rate limits of sources. So the categorisation of sources based on reputability would be the better bet. It'd be miles ahead in contributing to safety than a feature that creates only false sense of safety through it only being a safety feature as it's guise when it's nothing more than blatant petty queerphobia at play.

The Issue on the original project on this: https://github.com/KotatsuApp/Kotatsu/issues/1391

### Acknowledgements

If by "store" you mean the "IzzyOnDroid repo", and by "you guys" the IzzyOnDroid team: the APK _you_ have built, signed, and attached to your releases here. As [our website](https://izzyondroid.org/) states:

> IzzyOnDroid curates free, open-source Android apps into an F-Droid-compatible repository. We distribute APKs built and signed by the corresponding developers—after scanning for safety and more, making the scan results transparent.

😉

The APKs our builders produce, are discarded after the build – they don't go anywhere. Those builds are just to confirm _your_ APK was indeed built from exactly the source you state, and nobody added or removed a thing (e.g. "supply chain attack"). So they are rather like a "specific scan".

```diff

```

Was that built from a clean tree at the tagged commit – or with local changes to the manifest? Next, `assets/sentry-debug-meta.properties`. Yours have more entries, and others:

```
# Generated by sentry-android-gradle-plugin
io.sentry.ProguardUuids=15b4c02c-837c-3605-8a86-ce53ddf8aedf
io.sentry.build-tool=gradle
```

versus

```
# Generated by sentry-android-gradle-plugin
io.sentry.ProguardUuids=20379f5c-a46d-3cde-9466-12a7f072cb08
io.sentry.build-tool=gradle
io.sentry.bundle-ids=d40beb29-57dd-4105-b2a8-9b8c5462bce5
```

Can you tell Sentry to NOT generate/include that file? I guess the differences in `classes.dex` might be caused by that, in turn causing the baseline to differ. Bingo:

```diff
 |: sget v1, Lio/github/landwarderer/futon/FutonApp;.$r8$clinit:I
-|: const-string v1, "https://fd9936db6078e313a9fe30ec5070bfc3@o4510583318183936.ingest.de.sentry.io/4510583326507088"
```

no counter-part in our build – most likely some variable set at your end, but not at ours. This means, this release won't make it to F-Droid – as RB will fail there, too.

Options I see:

* keeping Sentry from adding that file
* removing Sentry again
* providing a Sentry-free flavor for F-Droid and us to pick.

So 9.6.13 will not become available at F-Droid – and at IzzyOnDroid, while becoming available, will carry a "warning shield" stating that RB failed.

[See here](https://github.com/darriousliu/PiPixiv/commit/3985dfd5617997605812b89135b4e19430a1bf83) for what would need to be done. It's basically just disabling the Sentry Gradle Plugin, not Sentry itself, if I understand that diff correctly.

comments.author: bhoomik-codes
comments.body:
Thank you for the detailed feedback @PoonHarpoon and @onlyashd. We have addressed all points raised across both reviews and added proactive safeguards in commit `e273e62c8`.

### Summary of Fixes & Technical Decisions

#### 1. Chapter HTML URL Prefix (`novel_content://`)
- **Fix:** In `LnReaderNovelRepository.kt:131`, returned plain HTML directly (`url = html`) instead of prefixing with `novel_content://`. Updated the unit test assertion in `LnReaderNovelRepositoryTest.kt` to match.
- **Rationale:** `NovelReaderViewModel` feeds `page.url` directly to `NovelChapterContent.toHtmlFragment`. Removing the artificial protocol prefix prevents literal text rendering in the reader WebView.

#### 2. Dynamic Paging & Offset Fallback (`NovelPaginator`)
- **Fix:** Refactored `NovelPaginator` to track dynamic `nextPage` progression without hardcoded page sizes. When `RemoteListViewModel` drops duplicate items and produces non-boundary offsets (e.g. offset 19 or 9), `NovelPaginator` advances using the last known `nextPage` cursor instead of falling back to `offset / 20 + 1`.
- **Verification:** Added `testPaginationFallbackHandlesDeduplicatedOffsets` in `LnReaderNovelRepositoryTest` to verify that deduplicated offsets reliably request the next page without loops or premature pagination termination.

#### 3. QuickJS Runtime Lifecycle & Memory Leak Fix
- **Fix:**
  - `LnReaderNovelRepository` no longer holds a direct static `LnPluginRuntime` reference. Instead, it injects `LnPluginRuntimeManager` and resolves the runtime dynamically on each operation via `runtimeManager.getRuntime(plugin)`.
  - In `LnPluginRuntime`, added an explicit `@Volatile private var isClosed` flag. Calling `close()` acquires the runtime `mutex` on `Dispatchers.IO`, sets `isClosed = true`, and cleanly shuts down the QuickJS engine.
  - `ensureInitialized()` checks `if (isClosed) throw IllegalStateException("LnPluginRuntime[$pluginId] is closed")`, guaranteeing that a closed runtime cannot restart an orphaned context outside the manager.
  - On plugin update or uninstall, `LnPluginManager` invokes `runtimeManager.closeRuntime(pluginId)`, ensuring any cached repository picks up the newly updated script or fails gracefully if uninstalled.

#### 4. Default User-Agent & Network Fallback
- **Fix:**
  - Switched `LnPluginRuntimeManager` and `LnPluginRuntimeFactory` injection from `@BaseHttpClient` to `@MangaHttpClient`, applying `CommonHeadersInterceptor`.
  - Added modern mobile browser `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT` fallback in `ln_env.js` and `LnPluginRuntime.executeNativeFetch` when requests omit `User-Agent`, resolving 403s on Cloudflare/WAF-protected novel sites (e.g. BoxNovel, NovelBin).
  - Ensured relative fetch paths (e.g. `fetch('/api/...')`) automatically prepend the plugin's base site URL.

#### 5. Timeout & Cancellation Handling
- **Fix:** Replaced `withTimeout` with `withTimeoutOrNull(PLUGIN_TIMEOUT_MS) ?: throw IllegalStateException("Plugin evaluation timed out after 30s")` in `LnPluginRuntime.evaluateAsyncString`.
- **Rationale:** Prevents `TimeoutCancellationException` from being swallowed as a coroutine job cancellation, ensuring plugin timeouts surface clear error messages in the UI.

#### 6. Architecture & Code Style Touch-ups (@onlyashd)
- **`AppRouter.kt:230`:** Imported `NovelPluginsManagerActivity` and simplified to `startActivity(NovelPluginsManagerActivity::class.java)`.
- **`ExploreViewModel.kt:274`:** Simplified suggestion stream filtering and removed unnecessary destructuring.
- **Repository Cleanliness:** Reverted `.gitignore` and removed local build scripts from the workspace.

---

### Clarifications & Trust Model

#### Why `LnPluginManager` is `@Singleton`
`LnPluginManager` manages the persistent registry of installed community plugins. It is shared across multiple disjoint Android components and lifecycles:
1. **Explore Screen:** `ExploreViewModel` observes plugin state to display novel sources in Explore tabs.
2. **Sources Repository:** `MangaSourcesRepository` reads installed plugins to populate the sources list.
3. **Repository Resolution:** `MangaRepository.Factory` resolves plugin sources into `LnReaderNovelRepository` instances.
4. **App Backup:** `AppBackupAgent` queries installed plugins during backup/restore operations.

Scoping `LnPluginManager` to an Activity would force repeated disk reads, drop plugin state on orientation changes/navigation, and prevent injection into repositories and backup agents. Its singleton lifecycle mirrors `MihonExtensionManager`.

#### Sandboxing & Security Model
To address the concern regarding plugin script execution:
1. **Engine-Level Sandboxing:** Unlike Mihon extensions (which run compiled Android APK DEX code with full access to Android JVM reflection, local files, SQLite, and system permissions), LNReader plugins are pure JavaScript executed in an embedded QuickJS engine. QuickJS has **zero** OS bindings, no Node.js filesystem (`fs`) or process APIs, and no Android JNI access.
2. **Strict Bridge Surface:** The only bridges exposed to QuickJS are logging, plugin-scoped `SharedPreferences`, and HTTP fetch via OkHttp.
3. **URL Scheme Restrictions:** `executeNativeFetch` strictly validates URLs to `http://` and `https://`, blocking arbitrary URI schemes (`file://`, `content://`).
4. **XSS & WebView Sanitization:** All chapter HTML is sanitized with Jsoup `Safelist.relaxed()` before reaching the reader WebView, stripping all `<script>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<iframe>`, and `on*` DOM event listeners.
5. **Explicit Opt-in:** Plugins are never automatically downloaded; users explicitly choose community plugins from the repository catalog.

All JVM unit tests pass (`./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`) and the debug APK builds successfully (`./gradlew assembleDebug`).

comments.author: PoonHarpoon
comments.body:
A few follow-ups on `e273e62`. The paging and leak fixes look good, and none of these block on their own.

**1. Drop the hardcoded Chrome 120 User-Agent** (`ln_env.js:186`, `:200`; `LnPluginRuntime.kt:78`, `:276-279`)
The shim always adds its own User-Agent, so `CommonHeadersInterceptor` never applies the app's, which comes from the device WebView and stays current. For the same reason, the Kotlin fallback never runs. A Cloudflare clearance cookie only works with the User-Agent it was issued to, so a fixed string would also stop WebView clearance being reused. Removing both lets the interceptor fill it in, and plugins that set their own still win.

**2. `close()` blocks install and uninstall** (`LnPluginRuntime.kt:407-415`)
`runBlocking` waits for any running plugin call, so the install spinner can sit for about 30 seconds, or forever if a plugin is stuck in a synchronous loop. Suggest setting `isClosed` immediately and closing QuickJS in a background scope:
```kotlin
override fun close() {
    isClosed = true
    closeScope.launch { mutex.withLock { quickJs?.close(); quickJs = null } }
}
```
quickjs-kt 1.0.5 can't interrupt a stuck loop. Newer versions appear to support it (`evaluationTimeoutMillis`, `interruptEvaluation()`), so that's worth checking as a follow-up.

**3. A call in flight during an update fails once** (`LnReaderNovelRepository.kt:30-31`, `LnPluginRuntime.kt:88-91`)
If an update lands between getting the runtime and taking its lock, the call throws "is closed". The list's Retry recovers, but the reader shows "check your network". A dedicated `RuntimeClosedException` with one retry in the repository would cover it.

**4. Empty runtime after uninstall** (`LnPluginRuntime.kt:64-66`)
After uninstall, `getRuntime` builds a runtime with an empty script. `__futon_init_plugin("")` treats `{}` as success, so every call fails with a JS "not a function" error until the plugin is reinstalled or the app restarts. Adding `check(pluginScript.isNotBlank()) { "plugin not installed" }` in `ensureInitialized` would give a clear error.

comments.author: PoonHarpoon
comments.body: Each repository gets its own QuickJS context and nothing calls `close()`. Repositories are held only by `WeakReference`, and quickjs-kt 1.0.5 has no finalizer in its JNI wrapper, so each collected repository leaks a native context. After a plugin update or uninstall, a cached repository also keeps running the old script. Could runtimes live in a singleton keyed by plugin id and be closed on update and uninstall? The same applies to the construction at line 170.

comments.author: PoonHarpoon
comments.body:
The paginator fixes normal paging, but `offset / 20` is still the fallback at line 155. `RemoteListViewModel` sends the de-duplicated list size, so a single duplicate misses the map. At 10 per page, a duplicate on page 2 gives offset 19, which maps back to page 2; every result is then a duplicate and the list ends.

Recommend keeping the offset lookup and replacing the `/ 20` fallback with the last known next page. Because of known progress regressions in other places of Futon, I'd keep this fix inside `NovelPaginator` rather than changing the shared paging code.

comments.author: PoonHarpoon
comments.body:
The manager is a big improvement. One gap is left: `LnReaderNovelRepository` keeps the runtime in a field (line 26), and `Factory` can keep returning that repository after an update or uninstall. `close()` only clears the context, so `ensureInitialized` (line 85) builds a new one from the script captured at construction. That context is outside the manager, so it runs the old script and never gets closed.

Could the repository get its runtime from `LnPluginRuntimeManager` on each call, and could a closed runtime throw instead of restarting, with `close()` taking `mutex`?

comments.author: PoonHarpoon
comments.body:
The promise handling looks good. A few things to be aware of with the 30-second limit at line 224, though this can stay as is if you prefer:
- It covers the whole plugin call, so a plugin walking many chapter-list pages shares one budget and restarts from zero on retry. I haven't measured how often real novels hit this.
- `withTimeout` throws `TimeoutCancellationException`, which counts as a cancellation, so code that rethrows cancellations can hide the timeout from the user. `withTimeoutOrNull` plus a normal error would avoid that.
- It can't stop a synchronous infinite loop in a plugin, which would need an interrupt hook. That should be rare.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #146 from PoonHarpoon/fix/smart-resume-update-timeout

Keep smart resume working when the reader opens before chapters refresh
commits.author: PoonHarpoon

commits.message:
fix(reader): wait for chapter updates before smart resume decides

Opening the reader before the details screen finished refreshing skipped smart
resume. The manga handed to the reader carries no chapters, so the reader
starts from the stored list, which does not have the new chapter yet. Without
"Wait for chapter updates" it decided on that list, found no next chapter and
kept the finished one for good.

Drop that setting and always wait, but only when an advance is possible: the
saved chapter is finished and was the last one at the reader's last save, and
the known list has nothing after it. A known successor advances at once, and
every other start still opens immediately.

A new "Chapter update timeout" (1-120 s, default 15) bounds the wait. On
timeout or a failed update, the stored list is checked again, since the
details screen may have refreshed it meanwhile, before falling back to the
saved position. A timeout also shows a message.

The opened chapter is now found again in the updated list when the source has
given it a new id, using the matching history recovery already does, so a
renumbered list no longer blocks the advance.
